purpose: dated to the day of Herānandarāja Juju's Anantavrata observance (Anantacaturdaśī); possibly copied for that vrata
notes: The colophon does not name a scribe. The Newari line 'śrīherānandarāja jujuyā śrīanantavrata goyā dina' only marks the date as the day of Herānandarāja Juju's Anantavrata. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Herānanda juju' is not supported by the colophon; he may have been the sponsor or beneficiary of the copy, but the text does not say so. The catalogue's 'SAM 1282' conflicts with the colophon's 'saṃvat 944'. The colophon's date is internally consistent: Bhādra śukla 14 is Anantacaturdaśī, and NS 944 (≈ 7 Sept 1824 CE) fell on a Tuesday, matching roja 3. 'juju' is a Newari honorific for a king or lord; in 1824 (Shah period) it is probably honorific here. 'rāja' may be either part of the name or a title.
